title: ESLint V9 - Typed
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

Add typed rules check to ESLint v9. 

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [ ] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://mermaid.js.org/community/contributing.html)
- [ ] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests.
- [ ] :notebook: have added documentation. Make sure [`MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION`](https://mermaid.js.org/community/contributing.html#update-documentation) is used for all new features.
- [ ] :bookmark: targeted `develop` branch
author: sidharthv96

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
Should we switch this to a template string instead?

```suggestion
      return `translate(${labelArcGenerator.centroid(datum)})`;
```
comments.label_reasoning: Suggesting use of template literals instead of string concatenation, which is a JavaScript/TypeScript idiomatic convention.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: The problem is that the `.centroid` function returns `[number, number]`. So we should look into this properly, maybe when it creates an issue. Even if we use template string, it'll throw another error.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests switching to a template string with a specific code suggestion.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
It looks like this function acts differently if `text` is an empty string `''`. Is this expected behaviour? If not, we should replace this with:

```suggestion
  if (text === undefined) {
```
comments.label_reasoning: The condition behaves differently for empty string vs undefined, which may not be the intended behavior — a logic/semantic correctness issue.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags a potential bug with empty string behavior and provides a specific code suggestion to fix it.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
This seems like it might be a bug to me.

Are one of these values potentially not a `number`?
comments.label_reasoning: Reviewer suspects a potential bug where values may not be numbers, indicating a type or logic correctness issue.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body:
That's because msgModel has a default of null, so these values have an inferred type of `never`. 
Adding types should fix it.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags a potential bug and asks whether a value might not be a number, implying a fix is needed.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
I think:

- `egdes` is probably a typo of `edges`, so should be fixed in the code where it occurs.
- `affedcting` is probably a typo of `affecting`.
- `handdrawn` is probably a typo of `hand-drawn` or `hand drawn`.
comments.label_reasoning: Typos in code identifiers and comments reduce clarity and readability; naming/spelling issues in variable names and documentation.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: Will change, I was trying to get errors to 0 without any actual changes. 😆

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: We'll have to keep handdrawn, as it's used in `handdrawnSeed: 0,`

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Identifies typos and requests they be fixed in the codebase.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
```suggestion
  await mkdir('stats', {recursive: true});
```

Setting `options.recursive = true` will also ignore errors if the directory already exists, see https://nodejs.org/dist/latest-v16.x/docs/api/fs.html#fspromisesmkdirpath-options
comments.label_reasoning: The suggestion is to correctly use the `mkdir` API with `recursive: true` to handle the case where the directory already exists, avoiding an error from incorrect API usage.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Provides a specific code suggestion to add recursive: true to mkdir call.
